architecture.separation: Dedicated daemon, database, sockets, and OS identity; no Publication Broker embedding or shared writable state.

audit.contents: Authenticated peer UID, capability, request digest, affected identifiers, previous and new stopEpoch where applicable, result code, timestamp, and transaction identifier.
audit.integrity: Append-only through daemon APIs; audit and successful state mutation are atomic. Failed requests receive failure audit entries in separate bounded transactions without fabricating state changes.

authorizationGrants.approverUid: Always authenticatedPeerUid from SO_PEERCRED; caller-provided approverUid is rejected.
authorizationGrants.binding: Grant binds exactly to grantId, authorization-envelope digest, subject, action, resource, parameters digest, trusted evidence digests, councilId, councilEpoch, issuedAt, expiresAt, issuance stopEpoch, maximum use count of one, and decision ALLOW_ONCE. No wildcard, prefix, implicit default, or post-issuance rebinding is permitted.
authorizationGrants.checks: All referenced evidence and Council epochs must already be trusted; timestamps and bounds are validated; frozen AuthorizationEnvelope stopEpoch remains a JSON integer within the safe-integer domain.
authorizationGrants.issuance: ADMIN socket only; exact UID in grantAdministrators.
authorizationGrants.revocation: A grant is invalid when expired, mismatched, explicitly revoked, already consumed, or its issuance stopEpoch differs from the current global stopEpoch.

ADMIN.changeUidPolicy: no RPC; root configuration management only

allowed: verify envelope/grant status without consuming it

consumeOnce.future: Any V1D checkAndConsume interface is dormant and requires a separate approved ADR defining its caller identity, effect boundary, replay behavior, and deployment wiring. V1C deployment tests must prove no such consumer or route exists.
consumeOnce.state: Schema reserves an atomic unused-to-consumed transition and audit record under a unique grantId constraint.
consumeOnce.v1cExposure: No production socket exposes checkAndConsume, and no production component may invoke it or translate any grant into an external, publication, filesystem, network, subprocess, actuator, or other execution effect.

councilRegistry.model: Trusted CouncilEpochRegistry keyed by exact councilId and epoch, containing validated council public keys, algorithm identifiers, validity bounds, and status.
councilRegistry.mutation: ADMIN socket only; exact UID in councilRegistryAdministrators; authenticated UID recorded in audit.
councilRegistry.validation: Reject unknown algorithms, malformed keys, overlapping or regressive epochs, caller-supplied derived hashes, and mutations that would reinterpret existing evidence or grants. Corrections require a new epoch; referenced epochs are immutable.

evidenceBoundary.authority: ADMIN socket only; exact UID in evidenceImporters.
evidenceBoundary.failure: Malformed, noncanonical, untrusted, ambiguous, oversized, or unsupported evidence is rejected without creating a trusted evidence record.
evidenceBoundary.input: Raw evidence bytes plus strictly bounded declared media type and source metadata; no hash-shaped artifact is accepted as proof of content or trust.
evidenceBoundary.processing: authledgerd parses with pinned validators, verifies signatures against an existing trusted Council epoch, constructs the canonical evidence object, canonical-serializes it using the repository hashing serializer, computes all hashes internally, and stores canonical bytes, computed digest, registry binding, and validation result.

payload.excludedComplexity: No HSM, TPM, enclave, hypervisor isolation, M-of-N ceremony, Merkle-SMT, air gap, or distributed consensus is selected because the stated local single-machine threat model is adequately addressed by kernel process identity, exact-UID authorization, root-owned policy, filesystem isolation, and transactional storage.
failClosedConditions: Peer credentials unavailable or changing during RPC handling

filesystemAndDeployment.config: /etc/mihver/authorization-ledger and UID policy are root-owned and non-model-writable.
filesystemAndDeployment.data: /var/lib/mihver/authorization-ledger is accessible only to mihver-ledger and trusted host backup administration.
filesystemAndDeployment.models: Claude and Codex receive no ADMIN socket access, ADMIN UID entry, daemon identity, root authority, writable config/data path, or credential capable of delegation.
filesystemAndDeployment.publicationBroker: Has neither ADMIN socket reachability nor an ADMIN-listed UID. If granted CLIENT reachability, it receives verification/status data only and cannot consume grants.
filesystemAndDeployment.runtime: /run/mihver/authledger is owned by mihver-ledger with mode 0750; socket modes are recreated and verified at every start.

ipc.authentication: For every RPC, authledgerd obtains authenticatedPeerUid from Linux SO_PEERCRED. Caller-supplied UID, username, group list, approverUid, or forwarded identity is ignored and rejected where present.
ipc.authorization: Socket and directory permissions provide reachability only. Every RPC is authorized by exact authenticatedPeerUid against daemon-loaded root-owned UID policy; SO_PEERCRED GID and supplementary groups never grant capabilities.

clientSocket.purpose: Non-effecting status, verification, and audit-query operations only

stopEpoch.increment: Within one IMMEDIATE transaction, read the singleton row and update using a bound application-computed Number only after Number.isSafeInteger validation. If current value is 9007199254740991, fail closed with STOP_EPOCH_EXHAUSTED and make no state or audit-success mutation.
stopEpoch.readRules: Reject non-integer SQLite storage classes and values outside the domain before serialization or hashing.
stopEpoch.schema: singleton row id=1 with stop_epoch INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(typeof(stop_epoch)='integer' AND stop_epoch>=0 AND stop_epoch<=9007199254740991)

storage.engine: SQLite with WAL, foreign_keys=ON, synchronous=FULL, busy_timeout bounded
storage.transactions: Each registry mutation, evidence import, grant issuance, and stopEpoch increment commits its state change and append-only audit row in one IMMEDIATE transaction.

uidPolicy.modelExclusion: Claude and Codex runtime UIDs are prohibited from every ADMIN role and from root/mihver-ledger membership. Deployment validation refuses startup if a model UID appears in an ADMIN role.
uidPolicy.mutationAuthority: Host root configuration management only; authledgerd has no mutation API.
uidPolicy.validation: At startup and before each ADMIN mutation, open with O_NOFOLLOW, require a regular file, owner UID 0, group mihver-ledger, exact mode 0640, bounded canonical JSON, unique nonnegative integer UIDs, known keys only, and no writable parent path. Any failure makes ADMIN unavailable and emits a local service error; no cached permissive fallback.

proposalContent.summary: Adopt a single-machine, OS-isolated authledgerd with role-scoped exact-UID administration, daemon-canonicalized trust imports, bounded persistent stopEpoch, transactional grants and audit, and no V1C execution-effect consumer.

decisionQuestion: What exact V1C privileged architecture should MIHVER adopt for the Authorization Ledger, human R3 AuthorizationGrant administration, trusted Council/evidence import boundary, and persistent global stopEpoch register, while preserving strict privilege separation and guaranteeing zero execution-effect consumers? This is a NEW candidate (decision-5); prior candidates (decisionHash sha256:540531...b6e9f3, REJECTED by seat-openai; and sha256:0e63ea1a...246175c, REJECTED by seat-openai with two named blockers) are permanently closed -- do not resubmit either, cosmetically rename them, or reuse their architecture unless materially revised to fix both named blockers below.
evidence: MANDATORY FIX 1 (decision-4's valid REJECT): the frozen AuthorizationEnvelope schema defines stopEpoch as JSON-Schema { type: integer, minimum: 0 }, and this repo's canonical JSON serializer used for all hashing throws TypeError on any BigInt. stopEpoch MUST NOT be an unsigned 64-bit value with plain SQLite old+1 arithmetic (SQLite INTEGER is signed 64-bit; values above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER cannot round-trip losslessly through this codebase's JSON/JS-number path without BigInt, which is forbidden). Instead define the domain as 0 <= stopEpoch <= 9007199254740991 (2^53-1), stored as SQLite INTEGER with an explicit CHECK enforcing that bound, with fail-closed STOP_EPOCH_EXHAUSTED on increment from 9007199254740991 (no wraparound/reset/coercion/float approximation/BigInt injection). A different representation is acceptable only if proven lossless through the existing frozen hashing path with no schema migration.

MANDATORY FIX 2 (from decision-4's valid REJECT): SO_PEERCRED supplies only the peer's effective UID/GID, not a complete or mechanically reliable supplementary-group authorization set for typical human accounts. The candidate MUST NOT treat SO_PEERCRED-derived group membership as the authorization decision. Filesystem/socket permissions establish reachability only. The service itself must independently determine an authenticatedPeerUid from the kernel (SO_PEERCRED), and authorization must be an exact-UID check against a privileged, non-model-writable, root-owned allowlist (e.g. /etc/mihver/authorization-ledger/admin-uids.json or an equivalent), readable only by the daemon, fail-closed on invalid ownership/mode/format, with no caller-controlled UID and no Claude/Codex modification path.

MANDATORY: your candidate MUST NOT claim 'zero execution consumers' while also describing any downstream execution-tier consumption flow. ALLOW_ONCE/checkAndConsume may exist as privileged state only; no production component may consume it to perform an effect in V1C. A future V1D handoff must be described only as a dormant interface requiring a separate ADR.

MANDATORY: define mechanically enforceable privilege separation: process identity, OS user/group, ADMIN vs CLIENT capability split, filesystem ownership, IPC permissions, trusted-registry mutation authority, evidence import authority, grant issuance authority, and stopEpoch mutation authority. 'Logically separate' alone is insufficient.

Baseline: a dedicated privileged Authorization Ledger daemon (authledgerd) under a dedicated OS identity (mihver-ledger), structurally separate from the Publication Broker, with separate ADMIN and CLIENT Unix-domain sockets using filesystem permissions plus kernel peer-credential (SO_PEERCRED UID) checks re-verified per RPC against a privileged UID allowlist, SQLite/WAL transactional storage, a trusted CouncilEpochRegistry, canonical privileged-validated evidence import (never trusting caller-supplied hash-shaped artifacts), the stopEpoch from FIX 1, exact-bound AuthorizationGrants whose approverUid is the authenticated peer UID (never caller text), a consume-once ledger, and transactional audit -- ZERO production consumer of checkAndConsume/ALLOW_ONCE at V1C exit. Select a different design only if materially safer/simpler for MIHVER's actual local single-machine threat model.

Do NOT select HSM/TPM/enclave/hypervisor isolation/M-of-N human ceremony/Merkle-SMT state/air-gap/distributed consensus unless you name a concrete threat that simpler local OS-level privilege separation does not adequately mitigate.

Claude and Codex must never hold ADMIN capability or credentials, must never be able to create an AuthorizationGrant, register/mutate the Council trust registry, change the admin UID allowlist, or change stopEpoch, under any circumstance in your design.
Keep your JSON payload concise and concrete enough that a fresh implementation team could implement it without reopening basic trust-boundary decisions, but do not include chain-of-thought.
